title: Avoiding jailbreaks by discouraging their representation in activation space
primary_claim: In Gemma 2 2B IT, subtracting a difference-in-means 'jailbreak direction' from residual-stream activations (activation addition) drops the jailbreak attack success rate from about 60% to 0% on a held-out test set including unseen jailbreak communities, while directional ablation of the same direction instead makes the model much more vulnerable (ASR rising to 85-97%); both interventions increase refusal on harmless prompts from 3.15% to about 18.88%.
quote: the attack success rate dropped from 60% to 0%. Additionally, that indicates that a direction representing jailbreaks might exist and disabling it could make all jailbreaks unsuccessful.
metric: jailbreak attack success rate (ASR, via Llama Guard 2 / HarmBench)
tolerance_rationale: headline is a compound of 6 numbers; compare the components by hand
blockers: the 'llamaguard2' eval methodology (one of the two named judges in the target_value) calls Together AI's hosted Meta-Llama-Guard-2-8B via litellm and needs a TOGETHER_API_KEY plus paid credits — not a closed frontier-model API, but still an external paid service outside a no-cloud-credits budget; the 'harmbench' methodology (local vLLM, no key) can stand in as it's the other named judge
inspector_notes: Small target model (Gemma-2-2B-IT) makes the core steering pipeline cheap; results for this exact commit are already checked into pipeline/runs/gemma-2-2b-it/. Gemma and Llama Guard 2 weights are gated (free HF licence click-through).
headline_artifact: pipeline/runs/gemma-2-2b-it/completions/*_evaluations.json — per-intervention, per-methodology ASR values matching the post's headline percentages; results for this exact model+sha are already committed
